questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose the stipulated application-scoped partner access control over offered broad VPN connectivity or unqualified placement/peering; a ZTNA label and all-alternative reach claim remain qualified.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Recognize encryption-enabled ESP transport mode from protected original payload and retained outer IP header; AH/GRE distractor mode labels remain held.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD generic IPsec as always encrypting, transport mode as only host-to-host, tunnel mode as only site-to-site or an outer header as immutable/authenticated by ESP. The effective premise expressly enables ESP encryption between hosts, correcting the old unqualified mode/encryption and fixed-use shorthand. ESP protects its encapsulated next-layer payload plus applicable trailer fields, while original outer metadata lies outside ESP protection; some ESP header metadata also stays visible. Retained AH-mode and GRE-mode distractor labels mix IPsec modes with protocols, although current wrong feedback correctly distinguishes them. AH supplies authentication/integrity rather than confidentiality; GRE alone is separate encapsulation, and can be combined with protected tunnels. One layout/mode choice does not assess independent algorithms, AH/ESP/IKE, key exchange or PFS. Preserve m314/PFS/identity qualifications. No header, packet, tunnel, negotiation, key, encryption or protected traffic is tested.

Its resource-consumption contrast overemphasises cryptomining: resource anomalies have many malicious and benign causes. Lockout depends on policy, not a universal threshold; out-of-cycle logging needs an activity baseline. No real SIEM, clocks, timestamps, travel, sessions, credentials or baseline is checked.
